open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct and certify a deterministic strict refinement of \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}\) for the regime \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), or prove that none exists, after specifying the intersection-null statistics and the exact lattice-consonance predicate.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen closure handle does not define the statistics \(T_{\mathcal U}\), a Boolean consonance relation on tablewise decisions, or the meaning of a nondegenerate table. More substantively, the atom condition \(\lambda_H(o)\le\alpha\) does not pay for the baseline noncoverage already incurred by populations with order \(o\); the exact residual-slack inequalities in the partial result must all hold simultaneously. No feasible strict mask satisfying those inequalities and a specified consonance system is certified by the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced every deterministic baseline-contained refinement to binary deletion variables and used the established exact coverage characterization to derive necessary and sufficient populationwise size constraints. Checked the one-table, one-order deletion route: it needs the stronger residual-slack certificate displayed in equation (3), so the threshold \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) cannot complete the argument. A closed-testing proof cannot be checked until the local intersection statistics and consonance implications are fixed.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\mathscr H_m\) be the finite set of compatible arm--outcome tables with row totals \(m\), and let \(\mathscr W\) be the finite set of complete weak orders on \(\mathcal R\). Extend \(L_N(H)\) by zero when \((H,N)\notin\mathfrak J\), and define
\[
 b_{H,o}(\alpha)
 =\mathbf 1\!\left\{o\in\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H)\right\}
 =\mathbf 1\!\left\{\exists N'\in\mathcal N(H):
       \mathcal O(N')=o,\ p_{N'}(H)>\alpha\right\}.
\]
For every candidate count vector \(N\), put
\[
 \beta_N(\alpha)
 =\sum_{H\in\mathscr H_m}L_N(H)
       \{1-b_{H,\mathcal O(N)}(\alpha)\}.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\), this is exactly the design noncoverage probability of the baseline rule for a schedule with count vector \(N\); by \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\),
\[
 0\le \beta_N(\alpha)\le\alpha
 \qquad\text{for every }N.
\]
Now let \(d=(d_{H,o})\) be a binary deletion mask satisfying
\[
 d_{H,o}\in\{0,1\},
 \qquad d_{H,o}\le b_{H,o}(\alpha),
\]
and define the contained deterministic rule
\[
 \mathfrak C_d(H)
 =\{o\in\mathscr W:b_{H,o}(\alpha)=1,\ d_{H,o}=0\}.
\]
Because \(d_{H,o}\le b_{H,o}(\alpha)\), for every \(N\) and \(H\) one has the disjoint-case identity
\[
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_d(H)\right\}
 =1-b_{H,\mathcal O(N)}(\alpha)+d_{H,\mathcal O(N)}.
\]
Multiplication by \(L_N(H)\), summation over \(H\), and another application of \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\) therefore prove the exact equivalence
\[
 \mathfrak C_d\text{ has uniform coverage at least }1-\alpha
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \beta_N(\alpha)+
 \sum_{H\in\mathscr H_m}L_N(H)d_{H,\mathcal O(N)}
 \le\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }N. \tag{1}
\]
Consequently, after a precise lattice-consonance predicate has been expressed as a finite set \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{con}}\) of admissible masks, existence of the requested strict contained rule is equivalent to feasibility of the finite binary system
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &d\in\mathscr D_{\mathrm{con}},\qquad
   d_{H,o}\in\{0,1\},\qquad d_{H,o}\le b_{H,o}(\alpha),\\
 &\beta_N(\alpha)+\sum_{H\in\mathscr H_m}
     L_N(H)d_{H,\mathcal O(N)}\le\alpha
     &&\text{for every }N,\\
 &\sum_{H\in\mathscr H_{\mathrm{nd}}}\sum_{o\in\mathscr W}d_{H,o}\ge1,
 \end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
where \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{nd}}\) is the intended, explicitly specified set of nondegenerate tables. If strictness is required at the supplied test bed, the last line can instead be written \(\sum_o d_{H^\dagger,o}\ge1\). All coefficients in (1)--(2), apart from the externally fixed threshold \(\alpha\), are computable rational numbers: \(L_N(H)\) is a finite sum of the exact factorial masses, \(p_N(H)\) is a finite right-tail sum of the same masses, and \(b_{H,o}(\alpha)\) is obtained by finite enumeration over \(\mathcal N(H)\). Thus (2) is an exact response-table decision problem and never requires labeled-schedule enumeration.

In particular, a proposed deletion of one retained order \(o_0\) at one table \(H_0\) is uniformly valid if and only if
\[
 \max_{N:\,\mathcal O(N)=o_0}
 \{\beta_N(\alpha)+L_N(H_0)\}\le\alpha, \tag{3}
\]
with the convention \(L_N(H_0)=0\) off \(\mathfrak J\). The frontier condition \(\lambda_{H_0}(o_0)\le\alpha\) controls only the second summand in (3); it does not control the already-spent baseline size \(\beta_N(\alpha)\). Hence \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) alone neither supplies a feasible deletion nor verifies consonance.

proofs.proof_tex:
By Lemma \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\) and Theorem \(\texttt{thm:deterministic-order-atom-frontier}\), the finite atom thresholds satisfy
\[
0<\delta_\star\le \delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\le 1.
\]
Hence the assumed inequality \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\) implies
\[
\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}.
\]
Fix a compatible arm--outcome table \(H\), meaning \(\mathcal N(H)\ne\varnothing\), and put
\[
\mathfrak O_H=\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\}.
\]
The rule \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) is deterministic and table-measurable and, by hypothesis, is uniformly design-valid over all deterministic binary schedules in the stated class. Therefore Theorem \(\texttt{thm:deterministic-order-atom-frontier}\), applied using \(\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), yields both
\[
\mathfrak O_H\subseteq\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)=\mathfrak O_H.
\]
The assumed containment \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) consequently gives
\[
\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
=\mathfrak O_H
\subseteq\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)
\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H),
\]
and thus
\[
\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)=\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H).
\]
Because \(H\) was arbitrary, this equality holds at every compatible table. The baseline rule used here is itself uniformly valid by Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\).

For the sharper witness, fix \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\) and suppose
\[
\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H).
\]
The realizability part of Lemma \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\), together with the response-type construction \(\texttt{def:response-type}\) under the fixed-schedule and stratified-interference assumptions, supplies a deterministic binary schedule in the stated class whose response-count vector satisfies \(N^\star=N\). Under the exact first- and second-stage randomization assumptions, the exact identity in that lemma gives its design noncoverage probability as
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
\mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
\mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\\
&\qquad=
\sum_{\substack{H':(H',N)\in\mathfrak J}}
L_N(H')\,
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H')
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every summand is nonnegative. The summand indexed by the fixed \(H\) is present because \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\), and its indicator is one by the supposed omission. It follows that
\[
\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
\mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
\mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}
\ge L_N(H).
\]
Lemma \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\) gives \(L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star\), while the present level satisfies \(\delta_\star>\alpha\). Therefore
\[
\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
\mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
\mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}
\ge L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star>\alpha.
\]
This is the asserted schedule-specific atom obstruction and contradicts uniform \((1-\alpha)\)-coverage whenever such an omission occurs.

Finally, suppose that a family indexed by every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) were uniformly valid, were contained in \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha\) at every compatible table, and were strictly contained at some compatible table at every level. Since \(\delta_\star>0\), choose \(\alpha_0\in(0,\delta_\star)\). The equality already proved at level \(\alpha_0\) rules out strict containment at every compatible table, a contradiction. The argument uses no claim about \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\), so the stated upper-level limitation is preserved.
